findings.title: Imported feed/article HTML is persisted without sanitization
findings.body: `import` creates posts with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns this content verbatim. `contents` comes directly from RSS/Atom feeds or a remotely fetched page and is neither sanitized nor escaped before becoming `post.cooked`; it also interpolates the unescaped source URL into an HTML attribute on line 13. A malicious article/feed item can therefore store script/event-handler HTML that executes for users viewing the imported topic (and in the embed view, which renders `raw post.cooked`). Sanitize imported HTML and URLs with the normal allowlist before storing/rendering it rather than bypassing the cooking pipeline.

findings.title: Remote import follows redirects without enforcing the allowed host
findings.body: The retriever validates only the host of the initial `embed_url`, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects and this method does not validate each redirect target or block private/reserved addresses. An unauthenticated caller can request an allowed-host URL that redirects to an internal service (for example via an open redirect on the configured site), causing the Discourse server to fetch internal endpoints. Enforce the host/address policy on every redirect hop (and reject private/link-local targets), or use an HTTP client configured not to follow redirects.

findings.title: Relative links without a leading slash are not converted to source URLs
findings.body: Despite the method's contract to convert relative URLs, it only rewrites `href` and `src` values beginning with `/`. Common document-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg`, `../article`, or `?page=2` remain unchanged. Once the content is displayed on Discourse, browsers resolve those URLs relative to the forum/embed URL rather than the original article, producing broken or incorrectly directed links and images. Resolve all non-absolute URLs against the full source URL (for example with `URI.join`).

findings.title: The success-path spec expects a retriever call that the controller no longer makes
findings.body: This example sets an expectation that `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` is invoked, but `EmbedController#best` now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` instead. The expectation is unsatisfied whenever this example runs, so the newly added controller spec fails rather than testing the asynchronous behavior. Update it to assert the queued job and its arguments.
